title: Spin a lazy Susan on a pantry shelf to bring the spice jar at the back to the front, then take it out
instruction: Take the jar with the red cap from the back of the lazy Susan and stand it on the counter mark in front of the shelf, without tipping any jar.
context: Cooks keep spices and small jars on turntables in cabinets and on pantry shelves; O*NET lists procuring food from storage and rotating stock among a restaurant cook's tasks, and the same reach-in is done in home kitchens daily. The shelf above is low and the jars stand close together, so the jar at the back is reached by turning the store, not by moving the jars in front of it.
setup: Positions in cm, x forward from the arm bases' midpoint, y toward the left arm, z up from the table top. A pantry shelf section (IKEA IVAR, 42 x 30 cm shelves, 1.8 cm thick) stands on the counter against the kitchen wall, its front edge at x 32, centred on y 2; the upper shelf's underside is 20 cm above the counter. On the bottom shelf, flush with its front edge, an OXO Good Grips 11 in lazy Susan (tray 27.9 cm across, 1 cm lip, usable 23.5 cm) turns on a ball bearing about (46.0, 2.0). Six 4.5 x 4.5 x 11.2 cm spice jars of 89 g (McCormick 2.37 oz size) stand on a 17 cm ring on the tray; the red-capped one is at the back, by the wall. The counter mark is at (24, 2), 8 cm in front of the shelf.
scoring: 0 if any other jar tips more than 15 degrees or leaves the tray, if the red-capped jar tips while on the tray, or if the tray is lifted off its bearing (all latched). 0.5 once the red-capped jar has come round, upright on the tray, to within 30 degrees of the front. 1.0 with, as well, the red-capped jar standing upright (within 5 degrees) on the counter mark (within 2 cm), no jar held and every jar moved under 2 mm and turned under 2 degrees over the last second.
reset_notes: Simulation: every part returns to its start pose at reset. Real trial, each time: turn the tray so the red-capped jar is at the back against the wall, stand the six jars on their ring marks, and clear the counter mark.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with real contact: the tray turns on a hinge with Coulomb friction (the bearing's friction torque is not published, so the demo is checked over 0.005-0.05 N m), the jars stand loose on it and are carried round by friction, and the hands turn it by pinching its lip.
